Currently selected: Clearer merge status and next steps Clearer merge status and next steps Smoother review and comment interactions Activity details Page layout and sidebar actions Try the new overview page and give feedback Your feedback has helped improve the new pull request Overview page since its November 5, 2026 public preview. Here’s what’s new! Clearer merge status and next steps Failed optional checks no longer make mergeable pull requests appear blocked. Previously missing merge requirements now show what needs attention. Readiness summary gives reviewers and visitors clearer guidance, including when no action is needed. Smoother review and comment interactions Checks and approvals now expand when clicked, instead of pinning a preview. Fixed overlapping previews and mobile interaction issues. Resolved review threads now collapse to keep completed conversations out of the way. Comments mentioning Copilot now better explain the action and selected model before submission. Activity details Force-push activity now links to the old and new commits so you can compare changes. Commit activity now includes timestamps so you can see when changes were made. Page layout and sidebar actions Source and target branches now stay visible on smaller screens. Edit links in the Development sidebar directly in Overview. title: Enterprise Live Migrations from Azure DevOps generally available - GitHub Changelog
excerpt: Enterprise Live Migrations (ELM) from Azure DevOps Services to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency is now generally available. You can move your repositories while your teams keep working, then…
body_excerpt: Enterprise Live Migrations from Azure DevOps generally available - GitHub Changelog Skip to content Skip to sidebar / Blog Changelog Docs Customer stories Try GitHub Copilot app See what's new Search Changelog Docs Customer stories See what's new Try GitHub Copilot app Back to changelog Release November 19, 2026 • 1 minute read Enterprise Live Migrations from Azure DevOps generally available Enterprise Live Migrations (ELM) from Azure DevOps Services to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency is now generally available. You can move your repositories while your teams keep working, then cut over on your schedule. Manage migrations through the portal or CLI: Choose a guided experience in the Azure DevOps portal or script your migrations with the Azure DevOps CLI. Pre-migration validation and lifecycle tracking help you identify issues and monitor progress before cutover. Cut over on your schedule: ELM continuously syncs changes from Azure DevOps to GitHub, so developers can keep contributing throughout the migration. When you’re ready, complete the move with a brief cutover at a time that works for your teams. Bring your development history with you: ELM syncs Git history, branches, tags, and pull requests, including titles, descriptions, comments, and user history. Your Azure DevOps branch policies migrate as GitHub branch rulesets. Keep using Azure Boards and Azure Pipelines: You can have ELM create the Azure Boards connection and rewire Azure Pipelines to your migrated GitHub repository, reducing manual setup after cutover. Your work items and pipeline definitions stay in Azure DevOps. Ready to start your migration journey?
